snail-inspired pump for microplastics

junior independent work, princeton mae · advisor: michelle dibenedetto · sep 2025 – may 2026

floating microplastics are hard to collect without churning the surface and pushing them deeper. apple snails pull particles along the water surface with a gentle undulation, so this project tests a pump that copies them: a flexible 3d-printed carpet that ripples as a helix turns beneath it.

  • 3d-printed and assembled the pump
  • drove the motor with an arduino and l298n driver, and swapped hand-counted rotations for an fft of tracking video to fix a frequency calibration that drifted as the motor heated
  • cut surface glare with blackout cloth, which doubled camera capture from 45 to 90 fps, and calibrated the camera with a checkerboard in matlab

event cameras vs. a turbulent jet senior thesis

princeton mae · advisor: michelle dibenedetto · sep 2026 – now

event cameras don't take frames; each pixel reports only when its brightness changes, which makes them very fast. my thesis compares a prophesee event camera with a basler scientific frame camera for planar laser-induced fluorescence (plif) imaging of a turbulent round jet, to see what each can tell us about turbulence statistics and structures.

next up: turbulence statistics from the dye concentration, then identifying coherent structures as a core part of the project.

end-to-end deep learning for driving

course project · open the notebook

  • trained cnn and lstm models to predict steering angle straight from camera images, following nvidia's end-to-end approach
  • used left, center and right cameras, labeling the side views with a steering correction so the model learns to recover toward the center of the lane
